inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: This “15-point ceasefire plan” sent to Iran through Pakistan looks like a carefully staged blame operation, not a serious effort to stop the fighting. The terms appear designed to be rejected so the people pushing them can claim Iran chose escalation. Iran’s five counter-conditions put the actual stakes—ending aggression, compensation, and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz—where they can’t be ignored. And Israel’s skepticism, alongside its insistence on pre-emptive strikes, makes the public peace talk look like cover: negotiations on the powerful players’ terms, with escalation still on the table and responsibility assigned in advance.
